Everything about Hubbard's later Chicago life was documented here and the date he first came was a fact everyone knew and nothing in data/sources/ stated, so it was carried as a conjecture citing nothing and left visibly empty rather than quietly filled: it was the case AGENTS.md rule 1 exists for. Hurlbut's American Fur Company chapter, read for T-0575 and cited by this record since T-0594, closes it - Montreal 13 May 1818, Mackinaw 4 July, Chicago the last day of October or the first of November - and the asymmetry that was worth leaving visible is now a smaller and more interesting one. The sentence is the COMPILER'S, not the man's: it stands outside the quotation marks in which Hubbard speaks four lines later, so a date this project had no source for at all now has a source of 1881 at rung 4, and the record says both things on its face rather than letting the citation look like an attestation. WHAT T-0753 ADDED, AND THE ONE THING IT COULD NOT. The same sentence carries more than the date T-0594 spent, and the rest of it is now on the card: `origin` reads "Windsor, Vermont, by way of Montreal" rather than the "Montreal" a careless reading of the field would have written, and the person carries a `birth_year` of 1802 with the birthplace in its note, both at the inferred grade the rung-4 layer supports and both corroborated by the man's own Calumet Club register entry of 1879. THE PARENTS WERE THE PART THAT DID NOT FIT, AND T-0849 RULED WHERE THEY GO. Hurlbut names Elizur and Abigail (Sage) Hubbard, and this dataset held no structure for them: the only relationship structure it has is the household-level `kin[]` block ratified on 2026-09-05, whose rows are reciprocal between two households IN THIS DATASET, and Hubbard's parents were living in Montreal, were never in this scene, and have no household here. T-0849 set out two readings - leave parentage outside the town as evidence, or invent an external kin row with `household` null - and on 2026-09-10 chose the first, on the ground that both rules `kin[]` enforces are rules about the FAR END. The inverse must be legal; the mirror row must exist. A row with no far end is not a weaker kin row, it is one with the entire checked part removed, and a graded name with nothing checking it is a note. The second reading would also have made every genealogical name in the corpus eligible for a residents layer that reconstructs a town on one day. SO THEY ARE A NOTE, AND THEY ARE ON THE CARD: the `origin` note above names them at inferred, under this record's own Hurlbut citation, which is the idiom the `birth_year` note uses for the birthplace and hh_harmon_elijah_d and hh_porter_jeremiah use for theirs. docs/PROVENANCE.md carries the rule for the next fact that has no field, and tools/validate.py now refuses a null-household kin row in the ruling's own words rather than reporting a household that failed to resolve - a message that would send a later run off to mint a Montreal household, which is the wrong answer twice over. persons.name: Augustine Deodat Taylor
persons.note: AN ARRIVAL WITH A MONTH, WHICH ONLY SIX HOUSEHOLDS IN THIS PARCEL HAVE. He is also the man whose name is attached in the Chicago literature to the first balloon-frame building - St Mary's - and this record makes no claim about that, because Andreas calls him the architect and says nothing about the framing method. HE IS IN THE DATASET BECAUSE THE 1835 TOWN CANNOT BE BUILT WITHOUT HIS TRADE. Andreas's roster is the only list this project holds that names artisans at all, and every name on it is a documented alternative to an inferred one. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “TAYLOR A D”, 1836-06-23 to 1836-06-28: 2 lots in the platted town — lot 2 of block 42 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L2BL42CHIOT, as printed); lot 8 of block 6 in the town the register codes CHI (L8BL6CHI, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $5430.00 (ls1482, ls1483). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $5430.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: TAYLOR A D matches Augustine Deodat Taylor: the forename names Augustine Deodat Taylor of the 7 people of this surname, and the forename agrees as an initial only. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. Taylor,” (f1839_v0044, printed page 41, ward 1, voting for William B. Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Taylor, Miss Anna M. | Letter, | January 29, 1890.” (second_presb_0334, printed page 172), admitted 1890-01-29 by letter. These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 10 times, as “TEMPLE JOHN T”, “TEMPLE J T”, 1833-10-22 to 1836-06-21: 2 lots in the platted town — lot 4 of block 20 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L4BL20CHIOT, as printed); lot 6 of block 20 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L6BL20CHIOT, as printed) and 8 parcels of the school section — BL103 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL110 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL111 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL112 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL17 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL76 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL77 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL99 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read, 30.31 acres stated in all, for $21107.00 (ls0353, ls0354, ls0355, ls0356, ls0357, ls0358, ls0359, ls0360, ls1505, ls1506). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. Ground inside the town is nearer to this reconstruction than a quarter-section is, and it is still a purchase: the register names a purchaser and never an occupant, and nothing here puts this person on that ground. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $20000.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. A wife who is counted gets a person record with no forename; four children who are counted get ONE record whose name states the count. Neither is inflated into individuals and neither is dropped.
